---

id: ch-k3f9
title: The Crossing
---
The ferry left Szeged an hour late. Ilka held the will on her knees and did not read it again; she had read it *enough*.

Aunt Bea was waiting at the landing in a coat too heavy for September. "You came," she said, as if it were an accusation.

"I said I would."

"People say things." Bea took the smaller bag and left her the larger one, which was, Ilka thought, **entirely in character**.

* * *

The orchard began where the road gave up. Noël was sitting on the gate with a pair of bolt cutters across his lap, and he did not explain them.
